issue_title: First-class single-platform mode: run the full loop with one AI vendor, no deadlock
problem_statement:
First-class single-platform mode: run the full loop with one AI vendor, no deadlock

## Requirement
The loop must run end-to-end — build, test, review, ux-eval, security, release, historian — with exactly ONE platform CLI installed (only Claude, only Grok, only Codex, or only Hermes). Cross-vendor review and the Devin supervisor are the preferred shape (docs/20/22), but their absence must be a documented degraded mode, not a deadlock or a silent skip.

## Current gaps
1. `loop.sh --reviewers` defaults to `codex,claude` and `second-opinion.sh` assumes other vendors exist; with one platform installed, `--escalate-after` either fails or skips.
2. L-005's fail-closed rule ("missing reviewer blocks merge") is correct fleet doctrine but undefined for single-platform: Tier B/C could never merge, or worse, agents improvise.
3. Nothing exploits the fact that one PLATFORM still offers multiple MODELS: the reviewer hat can run a different model of the same vendor (e.g. builder on the default model, reviewer via `claude -p --model opus` / grok's alternate model) in a fresh context — real generator/evaluator separation without a second subscription.

## Proposal: first-class single-platform mode
1. **Same-vendor, different-model review.** `loop.sh --solo-platform` (or auto-detect: only one runner CLI present) sets `REVIEWER_CMD` to the same platform with an alternate model + read-only invocation. second-opinion.sh accepts same-vendor reviewers instead of erroring; verdicts still land in `gibson/second-opinion.md`.
2. **Degraded-mode contract in docs/11.** Explicit table: what substitutes for cross-vendor review (fresh-context adversarial self-pass + different-model pass), and what tightens to compensate — proposal: in single-platform mode, Tier B review requires TWO independent fresh-context APPROVE verdicts (different model where available), and Tier C remains human-gated exactly as today (docs/14 G12, unchanged).
3. **No-deadlock rule.** Resolve the L-005 tension explicitly: single-platform review per (1)-(2) COUNTS as the reviewer being present; fail-closed applies only when the configured review path itself breaks mid-run.
4. **GitHub identity note.** The same-author approve problem (L-015/L-021) is platform-independent — the bot/service-account token (see reviewer-identity issue) works identically in single-platform mode and is the recommended pairing so branch protection stays satisfiable.

## Acceptance criteria
- On a machine with exactly one runner CLI installed and no DEVIN_API_KEY, `loop.sh --runner <x> --solo-platform` takes a Tier A issue from claim to merged PR with zero human touches and no skipped review (journal shows the review verdict and which model produced it).
- `--escalate-after` produces a same-vendor different-model second opinion instead of failing.
- Tier B merge requires the documented two-verdict rule; Tier C still queues for the human gate.
- docs/11 documents the degraded-mode contract and its compensating controls.

Refs: docs/11 (solo loop), docs/14 G12, docs/15 (escalation ladder), docs/20 rule 1, L-005/L-015/L-021 in memory/LESSONS.md. Complements the reviewer-identity and git-configure issues.
